To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two MAP kinase kinases have been purified from A431 cells.
two MAP kinase activators (MAPK kinases) have been purified and characterized from epidermal-growth-factor-stimulated A-431 cells.
two forms of a protein kinase, termed MAP kinase kinase, have been purified from epidermal-growth-factor-stimulated cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a MAP kinase kinase, an enzyme that activates MAP kinase by phosphorylation of threonine and tyrosine.
identifying and characterizing the protein kinase responsible for the phosphorylation of MAP kinase on threonine and tyrosine, which is a critical step in the activation of MAP kinase.
the identification and purification of MAP kinase activators, which are protein kinases that catalyze phosphorylation of MAP kinase on threonine 189 and tyrosine-190.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MAP kinase kinases are protein kinases that are able to phosphorylate the regulatory residues of MAP kinase in vitro.
the MAP kinase kinases are protein kinases that phosphorylate MAP kinase on threonine 183 and tyrosine on 185.
the 46- or 45-kDa protein is a protein kinase that phosphorylates and activates MAP kinase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MAP kinase kinases are protein kinases that catalyze phosphorylation of the activation loop of native MAP kinase.
the MAP kinase kinases are serine/threonine protein kinases, which are specific for the native conformation (and not the inactive mutant form) of MAP kinase.

the 46- or 45-kDa MAP kinase kinases from A431 cells are protein kinases that phosphorylate MAP kinase on threonine 190 and tyrosine residue 188, and that these kinases are activated by epidermal growth-factor treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MAP kinase kinase is a protein kinase that phosphorylates MAP kinase on threonine 182 and tyrosine184.

the MAP kinase pathway is a complex signaling system, involving multiple MAP kinase kinases, and that these kinases are likely to play an important role in the specificity and regulation of this signaling cascade.
two forms of MAP kinase kinase exist in mammalian cells and that these kinases are activated in response to mitogens.
